sasha: Poking at the Gemma-converted Llama3 quant model — nightly eval shows a perplexity spike on long-context tests. I think embeddings are getting index-wrapped during conversion.
kevin: Can you paste the failing log / minimal repro?
sasha: Here's the spot where inference prints odd tokens (trimmed):
```
2026-02-15 03:14:22,123 INFO token_ids: [102, 2093, 5021, 30522, 40012, 50002]
2026-02-15 03:14:22,124 WARN embedding_lookup: requested index 50002 >= vocab_size 50000, using index 2 (wrap-around)
2026-02-15 03:14:22,124 DEBUG first_tokens: "\u0123..."
```
This only shows up post-quant convert + tokenizer merge. No error, but indices are silently re-mapped to small indices which explains semantically wrong outputs.
kevin: Ugh. That wrap behavior is in the conversion script where we cast token_id to np.int32 then use it as index into embeddings; on some backends negative/oversized ids become modulo'd. Did you try asserting token_id < vocab_size after conversion?
sasha: I added an assert and it failed for ~0.12% of tokens on the testset. Those token_ids come from the custom tokenizer merge we ran to glue two vocab sources together.
nora: Quick idea: dump tokenizer.token_to_id for the merged tokenizer and check max id. `python -c "import json; print(max(json.load(open('merged.json'))['model']['vocab'].values()))"` — might show ghosts beyond embeddings matrix. Also check if tokens were appended vs mapped. :mag: 
eval-bot: nightly-eval: model=gemma-llama3-quant-v2, suite=long-context, ppl_base=12.3, ppl_new=18.7 (+51%), regression=True, seed=42
raj: Hypothesis: during tokenizer merge we kept original numeric ids from both sources which created sparse ids > target_vocab_size. When we saved the tokenizer we didn't reindex to contiguous range; the embedding matrix remained sized to target_vocab_size (50000). So lookup uses index % 50000 or backend-specific wrap. This matches the warn. We need to either reindex tokenizer to dense ids or build an embedding remap table.
kevin: Reindexing tokenizer sounds correct. But for quick mitigation we can create an explicit remap array of shape (max_id+1,) where remap[old_id] -> new_id or -1. Then we apply remap before lookup. Can you share a tiny script?
sasha: Paste applying remap to embedding matrix (numpy hack):
```
# remap_table: list where remap_table[old_id] = new_contiguous_id
import numpy as np
emb = np.load('emb.npy')  # shape (50000, 1024)
max_old = max(remap_table)
new_emb = np.zeros((max_old+1, emb.shape[1]), dtype=emb.dtype)
for old_id, new_id in enumerate(remap_table):
    if new_id >= 0:
        new_emb[old_id] = emb[new_id]
    else:
        new_emb[old_id] = np.random.normal(0, 0.02, emb.shape[1])
np.save('emb_remapped.npy', new_emb)
```
This preserves old numeric ids so runtime lookup works without code changes. It's a bit heavy but quick for canary.
kevin: That will inflate embedding table but quick to test. Can you run on staging canary? I'll watch.
sasha: Kicking off re-convert + remap now. Will post logs. @nora can you add a unit test to conversion pipeline for token ids > vocab_size case?
nora: Yup — adding test to conversion CI: asserts that tokenizer.max_id < embedding_rows OR conversion emits a reindex map file.
deploy-bot: canary/deploy started: gemma-llama3-quant-v2-remap @ staging (build 2026-02-15-1203).
sasha: Canary finished smoke: generation sanity checks look better, perplexity dropped from 18.7 -> 13.1 on the long-context suite. Still ~6% above baseline; likely need to reindex properly rather than remap-by-expansion. Posting diff in #eng-ml later. :white_check_mark:
kevin: Great. Followup: plan a proper tokenizer reindex + small migration script to regenerate embeddings with contiguous ids. Also add a fast path in runtime to raise on id >= vocab_size to avoid silent wrap.
raj: I'll own tokenizer reindex in the conversion tool. Will produce mapping file and add to model package metadata.
sasha: Thanks everyone. Action items: raj (reindex tool), nora (CI test), kevin (runtime guard), sasha (full re-convert + eval).
